title: The Baptism of Jesus
summary: There are only two paths: striving for a righteousness of our own, or the new covenant in the beloved Son, who writes God's law on our hearts.
exhortation: John the Baptist came preaching in the wilderness: "Repent, for the kingdom of heaven is at hand." He wore camel's hair and ate locusts and wild honey. Here was a man totally devoted to the mission God gave him, and not, from a human perspective, someone who would draw a crowd. And yet Jerusalem and all Judea went out to him and were baptized in the Jordan, confessing their sins. Why were they willing to humble themselves and repent?

It brought to mind the prophecy of the new covenant in Jeremiah 31: "I will put my law within them, and I will write it on their hearts. And I will be their God, and they shall be my people... For I will forgive their iniquity, and I will remember their sin no more." The people flocked to John's message of repentance because they needed a law written on their hearts. They needed more than an external law they could try to keep to earn their righteousness, because that wasn't working.

But some still believed they could achieve a righteousness of their own. When John saw the Pharisees and Sadducees coming, he called them a brood of vipers and warned that the axe was already laid at the root of the trees. The one coming after him would gather his wheat into the barn and burn the chaff with unquenchable fire. There are only two paths: repentance and the new covenant, or unquenchable fire for those who try to earn righteousness by the law. There is no third way.

Then Jesus comes to the Jordan. John tries to stop him: "I need to be baptized by you." Jesus answers, "Let it be so now, for thus it is fitting for us to fulfill all righteousness." The heavens open, the Spirit descends like a dove, and a voice from heaven says, "This is my beloved Son, with whom I am well pleased."

God's message is clear: this is my answer. This is the new covenant. My Son, with whom I am well pleased, will fulfill the promise of writing the law on your hearts, so that you respond not from man-centered striving but from a softened heart that loves the Lord with all your heart, soul, mind and strength. Left to ourselves, we would have kept striving, staying in ignorance and arrogance, thinking we could achieve an impossible righteousness. But God made the way, prophesied it, and here he is: Jesus, the Messiah, the Savior of the world.
prayer: Jesus, if you had not come, we would have been utterly lost. How grateful we are that you came and did what we could not do, what we had proved we could not do. You gave us new hearts and opened our blind eyes to see this great salvation.

Keep softening our hearts and opening our eyes, so that we don't pass it by today but glory in it and rest in it. Let us not strive in our own strength for a salvation that has been given freely. Let us work diligently and with joy, not to earn it, but because it is done. Thank you for saving us. Fill everyone watching today with the power and joy of your salvation. In Jesus' name, amen.
